chunks.title: Stages of vision & aspects of vision loss
chunks.tldr: Rehab reduces consequences, not causes — 'nothing more can be done for the eye' ≠ 'nothing can be done for the person'. Three processing stages: optical (refraction, media — acuity tests it, magnifiers fix it), receptor (retina — central scotoma needs a PRL; scotoma interference not captured by acuity, needs fixation training), neural (TBI, stroke, CVI — may see contrast but misinterpret it; vision substitution e.g. cane). Four aspects (WHO framework): organ structure (pathologist) → organ function (VA, field, contrast — ophthalmologist; 'visual functions') → abilities (reading, mobility, ADLs — rehab therapists; 'functional vision') → participation/quality of life (society). Patients start from the right ('I can't read'); doctors from the left. Measure binocular VA for function; assess reading speed, endurance, comprehension.
chunks.hook: Visual functions = how the eyes work; functional vision = how the person works.

cards.a: Visual functions describe how the eye performs (acuity, field, contrast); functional vision describes how the person performs tasks (reading, mobility, ADLs).

cards.q: Why measure binocular acuity for rehabilitation/legal purposes?
cards.a: People function with both eyes open; it reflects real-world ability.

chunks.title: Comprehensive vision rehabilitation plan
chunks.tldr: Ask: 'How does your vision loss bother you most?' — then refer, as for any other problem. Don't wait for severe loss; early adaptation eases later loss; break bad news with a plan. AAO checklist: reading, ADLs, safety (falls, crossing roads), community participation, physical/cognitive/psychosocial well-being. Observe task performance; questionnaires; assess mobility → orientation & mobility (O+M) instructor; signal impairment (white cane). Interventions: vision enhancement (optics, lighting, contrast), vision substitution (talking books, voice output, Braille, long cane), assistance (sighted guide, guide dog), coping (treat reactive depression; successful rehab is therapeutic), human environment (involve family, avoid over-protection, peer support), physical environment (declutter, fixed places, good light, contrast — mark step edges). Team: OTs, CLVT, COMS, CVRT; resources — AAO SmartSight, AFB, Lighthouse, Library of Congress talking books, VA blind rehab centres.
chunks.hook: Enhance, Substitute, Assist, Cope, Adapt the people and the place.

cards.q: Five areas in the AAO vision rehabilitation checklist?
cards.a: Reading; activities of daily living; safety; community participation; physical, cognitive and psychosocial well-being.
